Sports.title: Why Honda only realised the scale of its F1 problems in January
Sports.content:
Heading into Formula 1's major technical overhaul, expectations at Aston Martin were high. With a state-of-the-art factory in Silverstone, legendary designer Adrian Newey and a works partnership with Honda, all the ingredients for success appeared to be in place.

That may still prove to be the case in the longer term, but the start of the new era has proved far more challenging than anticipated. Mike Krack recently admitted that Aston Martin had barely been racing before the summer break, simply because the gap to newcomer Cadillac amounted to around one second.

That changed when the AMR26 received its first major upgrade package in Hungary, although the chassis is naturally only part of the story. Honda has also encountered numerous problems since officially returning to F1, ranging from vibrations that troubled the drivers during the opening weeks of the season to a significant deficit in outright performance.

Speaking in an exclusive interview with Autosport, trackside manager and chief engineer Shintaro Orihara explained that the full extent of those problems only became clear in January.

“So, probably at the end of last year, our position was not so bad,” he said. “Still, performance and drivability were in the development stage, but it looked okay.

"But in January, we realised that in some of the areas we found some, not issues, but we realised that performance was always up, down, up, down. So we found some performance, but then we also found some reliability issues."

Shintaro Orihara, Honda Photo by: EYE4images / NurPhoto via Getty Images

Because reliability is always a top priority, Honda had to take a step back on several performance gains to ensure reliability at that performance level. Naturally, that slowed down its overall development.

"In January, we realised that our performance and reliability would not be competitive,” Orihara added. “When we started running in Barcelona, we realised that our performance was definitely poor compared to the other manufacturers. And also, we found some issues on the battery side."

Those battery-related issues made the development process more complex. They cost valuable track time during winter testing, something that was especially painful given Aston Martin and Honda's need to gather data to recover from their deficit.

"So we realised that we were not in good position, maybe at beginning of this year. Last year, at end of last year, we already saw that we were not competitive, but we didn't expect it so bad," Orihara admitted.

What has been Honda's biggest challenge?

Part of the explanation is that Honda's current F1 project is very different from its successful years with Red Bull, something that ties in with the company's philosophy of transferring F1 knowledge to other parts of the company.

Another part of the explanation is, according to Honda, the complexity of the current regulations. Orihara stressed that there has not been one single stumbling block ahead of 2026, but rather the combination of all the changes introduced at the same time.

Honda Power Unit Launch

"It's difficult to say which component of the power unit is most challenging because in this regulation, everything has changed a lot,” said Orihara. “For example, MGU-K power changed from, let's say, [120] to 350 kilowatts. That is a significant change.

"But also on the internal combustion engine side, we have changed the fuel flow rate. So in this regulation, everything has been changed so much. So, a challenging point for Honda is just the combination of a lot of changes happening at the same time."

That means Honda is lacking outright power from its internal combustion engine, something the long-awaited Zandvoort upgrade is specifically designed to address. It is intended to be the first step towards reducing the brand's still significant performance deficit.

On the electrical side of the power unit, the emphasis is on efficiency. However, Orihara explained that the changes there have also had a major impact on drivability – one of the areas that has been a recurring topic for Honda and Aston Martin in the opening months of the season.

"Removing the MGU-H has also been quite challenging on the power unit side,” he said.

“Probably that is the most exciting point for power unit manufacturers. I have always been mentioning drivability. That is, maybe not mainly, but the majority of that is coming from removing the MGU-H.

"So that is a challenging point for us as a power unit supplier, to keep the boost pressure at a target. Again, it's difficult to pick one component that has been most challenging for us, but it has been the combination of all changes at the same time."

Although Honda knows that returning to the competitive level it is targeting will take time - a lot of time - it hopes to make a first step at Zandvoort. That upgrade is focused purely on improving the internal combustion engine and was already tested during a filming day at the Hungaroring.

Sports.title: Why McLaren has been coy about introducing its rotating F1 rear wing
Sports.content:
McLaren will race its version of the so-called 'Macarena' rear-wing concept – but not until an unspecified point in the future, according to team principal Andrea Stella.

It's understood that the reason for not rushing to race the new rear wing is not linked to Red Bull's well-documented issues with its similar design. Instead, McLaren is being cautiously pragmatic, since the rotating rear wing adds to the complexities of managing car behaviour as it moves in and out of Straight Line Mode (SLM).

McLaren planned to test its new wing in Austria but made a late decision to abandon the evaluation. It then waited until Hungary to run it for the first time in FP1 on Oscar Piastri's car, driven by Leonardo Fornaroli, before parking it for the remainder of the event.

Max Verstappen crashed at the Red Bull Ring and Silverstone, prompting his Red Bull team to temporarily shelve its pivoting rear wing based on suspicions that a delay in airflow reattachment when the wing returned to cornering mode made Verstappen's car unstable.

"I have to say it's been a complicated project," Stella told media including Autosport.

"Which was no surprise because when we saw Ferrari introducing the wing in Bahrain test and testing it in China in the first lap, [Lewis] Hamilton spun. And then it took a few more events to actually being in condition to race it.

"We knew it was going to be a complex project, so I have to say that our engineering department has delivered this project in a way that looks well-behaved – like the wing in terms of mechanical actuation, times of the actuation, because there's some limitations by the regulations, not only for aerodynamic reasons.

Ferrari was the first team to run its rotating rear wing, which operates differently to the McLaren and Red Bull examples Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

"And then the overall behaviour from an aerodynamic point of view, reattachment – so the time it takes for the car to regain the load, not only the load on the wing, the load on the entire car as driven from the wing.

"All this I have to say has been pretty consistent with expectation, so it's been a positive sign off of this concept and we look forward now to introducing this concept at some future events."

These concepts are a classic example of thinking-outside-the-box creative engineering that is possible for the first time this season because the regulations are relatively open. F1 first adopted the principle of legally shedding drag in a straight line with the Drag Reduction System (DRS) in 2011, which permitted the upper rear wing plane to flatten in prescribed areas of the track.

The speed and actuation procedure for this was clearly defined, along with the dimensions of the wing planes themselves. But under the new ruleset introduced this season, in which front and rear wing flaps can open in specified Straight Line Mode zones, the speed of transition from one state to the other is defined (within 0.4s), but not the means by which it moves between open and closed.

McLaren's pivoting rear wing is closer to Red Bull's than Ferrari's, in that it uses a central actuator to manage the rotation rather than having a mechanism built into the endplates. Also like Red Bull's, it pivots forwards rather than backwards.

The means of actuation gives it an element of air braking as it closes. The trade-off between the two concepts is that Red Bull and McLaren accept a degree of aerodynamic blockage from the actuator and its shroud in exchange for having a wider space between the upper and lower planes when SLM is active.

Ferrari's also has to take a longer path between open and closed because of the angle of rotation.

Verstappen shunted in qualifying in Austria, and a delay in airflow reattachment to the rear wing was cited as one possible contributory factor Photo by: Getty Images

One of the less predictable effects of the new regulations has been the shift in tyre loading during the transition between SLM being on and off. This is because the airflow doesn't reattach to the wing planes instantly, but takes fractions of a second to re-establish its path.

Teams knew ahead of the season that this would be a significant performance factor, but were unable to measure it accurately with simulation tools such as the wind tunnel and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD).

The true extent of the shifts in loadings, and their effect on car behaviour, could only be measured at the track.

This also applies to the theoretical benefits of the rotating rear wings. The airflow around the rear of an F1 car is tremendously busy because of the interaction between the car's aerodynamic surfaces and the turbulent wake of the rear wheels.

Simulating this with great accuracy is very difficult in the wind tunnel, where model size is capped at 60% scale and the wind is generally blowing in one direction. Historically it is difficult to access a car's aerodynamic performance when it's in a state of yaw (i.e. turning), or facing different wind directions. The different deflection properties of the model tyres, as well as their smaller size, also has a tendency to skew results.

Hence McLaren has done a lot of FP1 running with large aero rakes fitted behind the rear wheels to validate substantial bodywork changes such as the latest-spec floor, introduced in Hungary, as well as its pivoting wing. Practical measurements trackside are the real proof (or otherwise) of any theoretical gains.

"There was a question about comparison with Red Bull, but I don't think the wind tunnel is a major factor in terms of determining the aerodynamic behaviour in reattachment," Stella said.

"I think you can use some other tools for that, and then the most important tool, especially when you have this sort of complicated project, even from an aerodynamic point of view, remains what you observe at the track. So it was important for us to acquire data here trackside, because you would have never relied on a wind tunnel only for such a delicate project."

Sports.title: Why the FIA couldn't intervene sooner over F1's 2026 rules
Sports.content:
With the first Formula 1 season under the new technical regulations approaching its halfway point, the summer break provides a good opportunity to take stock. The 2026 rules, with their much greater emphasis on electric power, have sparked considerable debate both in and outside the paddock.

F1 insists that fan ratings – for example in its own Formula 1 Fan Voice programme – have been largely positive, but drivers have been far more critical.

Max Verstappen described the power unit regulations as "Formula E on steroids" during winter testing in Bahrain, while Oscar Piastri spoke at Spa-Francorchamps about the "self-learning elements" of the power units and "qualifying grids being decided by computers behaving or misbehaving".

Asked by Autosport whether the criticism from drivers over the past few months had been stronger than the FIA expected, Tombazis responded: "I think drivers are, by definition, quite demanding clients. I don't think we expected them to have a sugarcoat or to not speak their minds. So to say that it's been more than expected, no, I wouldn't say so."

The complaints from drivers about energy management, super clipping and algorithms were also in line with what the FIA had anticipated, according to its single-seater director.

"We did anticipate a lot of these things that they have complained about in the two years before the launch of the season. We did try to make some adjustments, but we failed with the governance that was in place," Tombazis said. "So I think it was realistically only to be expected."

Energy-starved circuits such as Silverstone and Spa-Francorchamps have highlighted the shortcomings of the 2026 regulations Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

FIA tried to listen to F1 drivers' criticism in build-up to 2026

If it had been up to Tombazis, the changes to the regulations that have now been agreed for 2027 and 2028 – to gradually move to a 60-40 split – would ideally have been introduced much earlier.

"I think it's a bit of a shame that we had to wait until we discussed things in May and get to a package for 2027 and for 2028. I think we could have ideally done that a couple of years before and then there wouldn't have been all of this discussion," Tombazis said.

Several drivers warned about potential problems with the new engine regulations before 2026. Verstappen was the first to do so publicly during the 2023 Austrian Grand Prix, when Autosport asked him about his initial simulator runs with the new engine formula.

That has perhaps created the impression that drivers were not listened to in the years leading up to 2026, but Tombazis insists the reality is different. According to him, the initial feedback was taken seriously, but the governance framework meant the regulations could not be significantly revised.

"When OEMs decide to participate as PU manufacturers, they sign a governance agreement that is binding towards all parties, so the FIA, FOM and the PU manufacturers. It's similar to what the Concorde Agreement does for the team side of things," Tombazis explained.

"And there was a separate governance agreement signed in 2022 in order to basically outline the requirements for the PU manufacturers during the years of 2023, 2024 and 2025. That is before the championship started because there's such things like financial regulations for the first time."

The FIA states that governance, even with new manufacturers such as Audi, has made intervention impossible Photo by: Pirelli

Among other things, that agreement stipulated that new entrants would not be allowed to spend unlimited amounts of money to develop their 2026 power units.

"If a PU manufacturer who was not participating in Formula 1, let's say Audi, they still had to be bound by regulations and not come to us and say, well, we're not participating, hence we can spend five times the money. That would be unfair," he said.

"So that's why there was a governance agreement that on the one hand forced them to be bound by the regulations, including the financial and operational rules and all of that."

At the same time, that document made it much harder for the FIA to reopen the regulations in the years leading up to 2026 without securing a supermajority.

"On the other hand it put limitations as to how much we could change things unilaterally as the FIA. And therefore any change had to be approved by a significant number of the PU manufacturers," Tombazis explained.

"So for the sort of changes we did [in May], we needed at least four of them to agree. And quite simply, four of them did not agree during the years when we discussed some adjustments."

Tombazis had hoped that the changes for the coming years could have been implemented sooner Photo by: Lars Baron / Getty Images

Challenges known since 2022, but races still entertaining

Part of the reason for that was that the reality of the automotive industry looked very different at the time, with manufacturers placing a much greater emphasis on electrification.

"Overall, it was always a challenging target to have a close to 50-50 power split between the two units," Tombazis said.

"But that was a very important position for the OEMs participating, and frankly having to decide whether they want to be in Formula 1 or not. Don't forget that if we didn't have them in, we would have just two power units in Formula 1, which I think would have been a bit of an issue. So that requirement to have a much stronger electrical part did create these difficulties."

Tombazis explained that the FIA had already become aware of these challenges in 2022, a year before Verstappen publicly voiced his concerns, but by then it was simply too late to fundamentally alter the regulations.

"As simulations came in back in 2022 or so, we knew there were these issues, but we were a bit too far down the line there to change things and some people had committed too much resource," he said. "So that left us slightly on the back foot at the start of the season, discussing that."

Tombazis concluded by stressing that, despite all of this, the races themselves have still provided good entertainment during the first half of the season.

Tombazis feels despite the problems with the F1 regulations, the racing has been exciting Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

"Now with that said, I think most races have been pretty exciting, I would say. There's been quite a lot of fighting," he said.

"I would even say that currently we still have, I don't know if I would go quite as far as to call it domination, but we do have a clear advantage for one manufacturer. And in the past when we've had that at the early start of the regulations, races have been very processional.

"Now I think, even despite the fact that Mercedes have been doing most of the winning, I think the races have nonetheless been quite exciting with quite a lot of changes and so on."

Sports.title: Domenicali resists Briatore’s call for sprint races at every round | Brief
Sports.content:
Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali will not move to add sprint races at every round next season, but still plans to hold more than the current six.

Alpine consultant Flavio Briatore recently argued for F1 to hold sprint races every week and, as is done in Moto GP.

Speaking in Liberty Media’s latest earnings update call for investors, Domenicali said limiting the number of sprint rounds gives them scarcity value.

“Sprint races is an opportunity that, first of all, started because we wanted to produce something that could create action on the track, creating leverage for the promoter and ourselves to create action on the tracks starting for the weekend,” he said. “We’re going to have more sprint races next year, yes. We’ll inform when we will announce the calendar, how many.

“The principle is very simple. This is also an opportunity to increment the revenue stream, for sure. This is an opportunity for us to have new deals, as we have already seen, and moving in this direction will be our future. We want to do in the right way because, of course, this will allow us also to make sure that the scarcity is a value.”

Formula 1

Sports.title: Antonelli says he ‘let pressure destroy me’ in mid-season slump last year | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli admitted he succumbed to pressure when he suffered a slump in form during the middle of his debut season last year.

The Mercedes driver went through a seven-round spell when he finished in the points just once – albeit on the podium. His dip in form coincided with changes to Mercedes’ car which he struggled to get to grips with.

“I had a good start to the season, then I had a difficult period,” said Antonelli in a recent interview. “In the European season I really struggled and in that moment I let the pressure kind of destroy me as well during that period.

“I felt like I was letting down so many people who had believed in me. Of course especially Toto [Wolff, Mercedes team principal], because he was the main one who took the decision [to promote him].

“Obviously I didn’t feel good in that period. I wasn’t doing well. But then I had a big meeting with the team after the European season and it kind of allowed me to reset and just start again.

“Then I slowly found my way back. I had a good second half of the season and that gave me confidence, being able to overcome those difficult moments and gave me the confidence ahead of this year. It also made me learn a lot about myself, not only as a driver, but as a person as well.”

Antonelli said the experience taught him useful lessons about coping with adversity. “Obviously [during] that European season, I think probably most of the things I did, didn’t help me at all,” he said.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“But also I learned about how my body responds to those moments, how my brain responds, what helps me to get back into the right focus, the right mindset, what helps me to stay 100% in terms of energy during the whole weekend. So how to manage myself with events, obviously the driving and everything. So I’ve learned a lot about myself and how as well to respond to difficult moments.”

Mercedes promoted Antonelli directly to their top team, in the seat formerly occupied by Lewis Hamilton, at the age of 18. Antonelli said making his F1 debut with a front-running team left him feeling depleted by the end of the 24-round championship.

“I was so drained at the end of the year,” he said. “Obviously the team did an incredible job in trying to protect me. But the learning curve – I think I’ve learned much more than if I would have done in a smaller team.

“The learning curve was incredible, it was like doing three years at once. It was overwhelming, physically, mentally, because I’ve made so many new experiences as well.

“Also, doing a full F1 season for the first time, you don’t really know where you’re going, what you’re about to face. Obviously the year prior to F1, I’ve been doing race shadowing and everything, but it’s not the same.

“When I was doing shadowing, I was watching, I wasn’t there on track doing the job. So I felt very overwhelmed at the end of the year. And it was good to have a bit of a break to just have a little bit of time to analyse and reflect on the year and understand what were the good things and why and why some things went not in the right way.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Having become the youngest driver to lead the world championship, Antonelli says he is trying to enjoy the position and the attention which comes with it, particularly in his home country.

“It’s like in any sport at the highest level, there’s always pressure and of course, being Italian, Italy has been missing an Italian driver for quite a long time and obviously also knowing myself because I’m Italian.

“We know how as Italians we can get very excited about things and how expectations can get over the moon. But obviously that comes with a bit of a extra pressure. But I’ve been enjoying, I have been enjoying. I think what I’ve been trying to do as well is to embrace the pressure and trying to actually shine under pressure.”

Formula 1

Sports.title: Norris vs Piastri: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The super-close contest between the McLaren team mates last year would have made for a thrilling world championship fight even if Max Verstappen hadn’t got involved.

Now in their fourth season as team mates, with a completely different type of McLaren to get used to, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri have been fairly well-matched on the whole. However in individual races their relative performance has varied, most notably in Hungary last weekend, where Norris was clearly much quicker.

Norris has been on a strong run lately, out-qualifying his team mate for the last five rounds in a row. Though it bears pointing out that Piastri missed first practice at the last round and was badly baulked by Lewis Hamilton when he began his final run.

It took Piastri until the third round of the season merely to start a grand prix, suffering a mortifying pre-race crash at home, then retiring before the start along with Norris in Shanghai. He rebounded magnificently at Suzuka and might have won had it not been for the timing of a Safety Car period.

McLaren have had further technical trouble since then: Norris had back-to-back failures while Piastri’s retirement in Hungary capped a frustrating race where a wayward backmarker had already cost him the lead. Piastri had a rough race in Canada as well, where both McLaren drivers paid the price for a tactical gamble which backfired.

It was therefore fitting that Norris delivered the team’s first win as F1 headed into the summer break. His 36-point lead over Piastri looks like a fair reflection of their relative performances given the various setbacks both drivers have suffered. The world champion holds the upper hand so far but Piastri is keeping him honest as always.

Sports.title: Hamilton vs Leclerc: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Does Lewis Hamilton have an eighth world championship in him? Has he not recovered from the blow of 2021 or did he simply never gel with the ‘ground effect’ cars of 2022-25?

Those hoping to see the seven-times world champion fight for another title will have drawn great encouragement from what they have seen so far in 2026. Last year, in his first season at Ferrari, he came off badly in comparison to Charles Leclerc , taking a 19-5 pasting in qualifying and making zero podium appearances to his team mate’s seven.

Hamilton has given full credit to team principal Frederic Vasseur for implementing the changes he needed to make a success of his transition to Ferrari, whether that has involved different brake material or swerving the simulator. On the face of it, it has paid off, and Ferrari now have two A-list drivers performing at their peak.

Leclerc is still shading Hamilton on average in qualifying, but the fight between the two has been much closer. Hamilton has delivered more consistently on race day, including that breakthrough victory in Spain.

Both drivers have misfired at times. Leclerc had a spate of errors including costly crashes in qualifying at the Circuit de Catalunya and during his home race.

Hamilton, meanwhile, has picked up a bad habit of incurring the stewards’ wrath, collecting a series of needless penalties in recent races. Though some may not have been his fault or were debatable calls, many others were straightforward, and he was fortunate to avoid a worse penalty for his yellow flag slip in Silverstone.

For all that, Hamilton is Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s closest rival in the championship at the summer break. “Has the time finally come for Hamilton to hang up his helmet?” we asked in May, in what already looks like one of the most poorly-timed polls ever featured on RaceFans.

Sports.title: Antonelli vs Russell: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Early in the season it seemed certain that whichever of the Mercedes drivers came out ahead would be crowned world champion. That remains likely, but the threat posed by rival teams has grown in recent races.

Little about Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s form in his rookie season indicated that 12 months later he would be beating his team mate quite as emphatically as he is. But heading into the summer break, Antonelli holds a valuable 59-point lead over the other Mercedes driver.

It’s a far cry from the situation around 12 months ago. At the end of the ‘European season’, Antonelli was 15-1 down against George Russell in qualifying. He ended the season still with less than half his team mate’s points tally.

But after a difficult mid-season, following a Mercedes upgrade which did not go as intended, Antonelli rebounded impressively with the end of the year in sight. He reached the podium twice over the final four rounds.

So while Russell’s season-opening victory in Australia looked like the shape of things to come, Antonelli shattered those illusions by winning the next five rounds in a row. He got the rub of the green at times – technical trouble hit Russell in qualifying at Shanghai and took him out while he led in Montreal – but he has also seemed fundamentally more at ease with Mercedes’ W17 than his team mate.

The unusually high rate of problems on Mercedes’ cars, and Russell’s particular problems with poor straight-line speed at Silverstone and Spa, have further complicated the picture. Antonelli’s car has not been immune, breaking down in Spain and breaking an aerodynamic component at Silverstone. Overall, Russell has probably had slightly worse luck, but not 59 points’ worth. Antonelli is leading this championship on merit, and Russell will have to dig deep in the second half of the season if he is going to avoid a painful defeat.

Sports.title: Featured Comment: How far is modern F1 like the ‘turbo era’? | Formula 1
Dina Thorslund Dominates Cherneka Johnson, Claims Undisputed Crown
Sports.content:
Constant pressure, relentless volume and clean combinations set the tempo early. The defending champion found no answers to slow the pace or mount a meaningful counterattack.

By the second half, Johnson needed something significant to change the direction of the fight. She never found it. Thorslund remained in command through the closing bell, completing a remarkably one-sided championship performance.

Johnson never established enough distance to disrupt Thorslund’s pressure, allowing the Dane to dictate exchanges throughout the fight.

The victory unified the WBA, WBC, IBF and WBO titles under Thorslund.

Her return to the top follows a difficult period outside the ring. Thorslund previously held the WBC and WBO bantamweight titles before vacating them in June 2025 after announcing her pregnancy. She later suffered a miscarriage.

A return in January 2026 brought Thorslund the WBC interim featherweight title before she moved back down to 118 pounds to challenge Johnson.

Johnson had collected the belts that became available during Thorslund’s absence and came into Saturday night as the undisputed champion. That reign ended decisively.

Emotional celebrations followed the verdict, with Thorslund sharing the moment inside the ring with her son after completing her return to the top of the bantamweight division.

Sports.title: Edgar Berlanga Campaigns For Jake Paul Fight
Sports.content:
Berlanga posted the poster on his X account with little explanation, creating the impression of a fight promotion without a date or venue. There has been no corresponding announcement from Jake Paul, Most Valuable Promotions or Netflix.

That makes the graphic look less like fight news and more like Berlanga advertising himself for one of boxing’s biggest paydays.

The idea isn’t new. Berlanga has previously pursued Paul and called for a contract when Paul was searching for opponents in late 2025. Paul ultimately went in another direction, fighting Anthony Joshua in December.

Berlanga remains one of the names associated with Paul’s next appearance, although a Tommy Fury rematch has received greater attention. Chris Eubank Jr. and Ryan Garcia have been mentioned as other possibilities.

Financially, it isn’t difficult to understand Berlanga’s interest. A Paul fight would offer considerably more exposure and potentially more money than most of the fights available to him in the super middleweight division.

Berlanga returned on July 26 with a stoppage of Steven Butler at Madison Square Garden. Rather than waiting for Paul’s side to come calling, he now seems intent on selling the matchup himself.

The poster may be fiction. The interest behind it probably isn’t.

Sports.title: Tamm Thibeault Dominates Robinson, Captures Three Middleweight Belts
Sports.content:
Thibeault used her height, reach, and quicker hands to control the action from distance. She consistently landed the cleaner punches while forcing the Australian champion to work through incoming fire to get close enough to attack.

Robinson pressed continuously, turning portions of the bout into a physical battle. Both women finished bloodied, with the new champion suffering a heavy nosebleed after a clash of heads.

Blood streaming down her face created a dramatic scene in the later rounds, but it did little to change the fight. Robinson absorbed punishment while continuing to press, yet she never found a sustained answer for Thibeault’s southpaw boxing.

The shutout win moves Thibeault to 5-0 with three knockouts. Her amateur career included a world championship, Pan American titles, Commonwealth gold, plus two Olympic appearances.

Emotion ran high afterward as Thibeault held her newly won belts while still covered in blood, sharing a respectful moment with Robinson, who dropped to 12-4.

Thibeault now controls one half of the middleweight championship picture. Kaye Scott owns the WBA and WBC belts and faces Claressa Shields on August 15 in Atlanta.

If Shields wins, an undisputed championship fight with Thibeault becomes an obvious possibility. The bigger question is timing. Five professional fights is very little preparation for someone with Shields’ championship experience, leaving MVP to decide how quickly it wants to make that jump.

Sports.title: Ray Robinson’s Hard-Fought Night Against Bobo Olson in San Francisco
Sports.content:
At 23, the Hawaiian-born challenger had developed considerably since his 12th-round stoppage loss to Robinson in October 1950. Fighting in his adopted hometown, Olson forced the pace, working the body instead of staying at range against Robinson’s superior speed.

The 31-year-old champion was making the first defense of the belt he had regained from Randy Turpin six months earlier. Delays caused by a back injury and his mother’s illness had disrupted his preparation.

Olson took advantage by making the middle rounds competitive. Robinson even went down on one knee during the 10th after missing a left hook and losing his balance. It was not ruled a knockdown, and Olson backed away as Robinson got up.

That was as close as the challenger came to turning the fight.

The final five rounds belonged to Robinson, who used his speed and footwork to take command down the stretch. A strong finish in the 15th sealed a unanimous decision, with scores of 86½-78½, 85½-79½, and 84½-80½.

Afterward, Robinson gave full credit to his opponent, calling the contest “as tough a battle as I ever had.”

The crowd of 10,033 produced a reported gate of $63,053. Robinson kept just $1 of his purse and donated the remainder to the Damon Runyon Cancer Fund.

Going the distance in defeat was far from the end for Olson. He captured the world middleweight championship in 1953, setting up two more fights with Robinson. Both ended with Olson being knocked out.

Sports.title: Terence Crawford Isn’t Really Retired, Believes Greg Hackett
Sports.content:
“I’m not believing that Bud is retired. I don’t believe Bud is retired,” Hackett said to MillCity Boxing.

Hackett pointed to the long history of fighters returning after lengthy absences. His argument is that Crawford hasn’t been away long enough for Ennis to treat him solely as a retired fighter rather than a potential future opponent.

“People don’t retire in a year and be like, ‘I’m done for real.’ They come back. I’m not going to give you the respect you looking for and then you try to come back. No, when you come back, I’ll be ready for you.”

Hackett believes the situation would look different if Crawford remained on the sidelines for several years, allowing Ennis to freely praise his accomplishments without considering a potential match.

“But right now, it’s too early. It’s too early to do that because Bud could say, ‘You know what? I could wake up one day, you know what? I’m bored. Let’s go get some boxing money. Who want to fight?’”

A Crawford return would immediately create lucrative options, and Hackett believes plenty of fighters would jump at the chance for that payday.

“So, right now, all I’m saying is it’s too early to take Bud serious on the retirement talk. It’s too early. Bud is a nasty individual. You think he really retired? I don’t think so.”

Crawford’s retirement leaves Ennis with no reason to chase him, but Hackett isn’t treating the announcement as permanent. If Bud changes his mind, Boots would still be there as a potential opponent.

Sports.title: Tim Bradley Thinks Haney’s Skills Scare Fighters, But Is It Really About Money?
Sports.content:
“You would think that a guy with tremendous punching power, right, you would think that everybody would try to duck that smoke like a Mike Tyson or something like that, but damn, you got people ducking Deebo Dev, who’s not the biggest puncher,” Bradley said on his YouTube channel. “I guess his boxing skills is what spooks everybody about Debo Dev.”

That interpretation gives Haney plenty of credit, but it leaves out an important part of boxing negotiations. Fighters who get an opportunity against a popular champion often expect compensation to match the occasion.

Keyshawn was rumored to have wanted approximately $5 million to face Haney. The WBO purse bid produced a considerably smaller payday. Top Rank won with an $8.55 million bid, which would have given Davis 25 percent, approximately $2.14 million.

If Davis went into the process expecting $5 million, receiving less than half that amount likely made the fight far less attractive.

Paro may have looked at his opportunity in similar terms. If his financial demands killed negotiations, that doesn’t necessarily mean he feared Haney’s jab, movement or defensive style. He may simply have placed a higher price on accepting the fight than Haney’s side was prepared to pay.

There is a major difference between refusing to fight someone and refusing to fight him for a particular purse.

Bradley sees fighters running from Haney’s skills. The failed negotiations may have less to do with fear than fighters expecting a major payday when their name is called for a fight with one of boxing’s bigger stars.

Sports.title: Dainier Pero Stops Aleem Whitfield In Third Round
Sports.content:
Pero took control early. Working behind a stiff jab from mid-range, he kept Whitfield from getting close enough to generate sustained offense. The 6-foot-5 southpaw mixed in hard shots downstairs to punish Whitfield whenever he tried to work inside.

The difference in skill showed early. Whitfield struggled to solve Pero’s reach, while the Cuban dictated distance without much effort. By the third round, the body work and clean punching had taken their toll. Pero continued landing with little coming back, forcing the referee to step in and stop the contest. Whitfield never found an answer for Pero’s accuracy.

A former Pan American Games gold medalist and Olympic competitor, Pero handled Whitfield like an opponent he had already outgrown. The early finish was convincing, but beating fighters at this level no longer offers much insight into where Pero belongs among the heavyweights.

At 26, he has reached the stage where stronger opposition is needed. The more revealing test will come against a heavyweight capable of taking his shots, disrupting his preferred distance, and forcing him to make adjustments.

Sports.title: Would Top Rank Risk Emanuel Navarrete Against William Zepeda?
Sports.content:
“Man, that’s CTE at its finest. It’s a bloodbath waiting [to happen],” Crawford said during the post-fight show on DAZN and TNT’s “The Fight.”

While Crawford envisions both men doing serious damage, Navarrete may be the one taking the brunt of it.

Navarrete moved up to 135 pounds in May 2024, dropping a split decision to Denys Berinchyk for the vacant WBO belt. He struggled to find his rhythm against the Ukrainian, looking far removed from the fighter who captured titles at 122, 126 and 130 pounds.

Zepeda presents a completely different style of threat. He gives opponents little time to rest or set their offense. Roach discovered that early as Zepeda stayed in his face and dictated the pace for all 12 rounds.

Navarrete never shies away from trading punches, but slugging with Zepeda at lightweight favors the naturally larger man. Moving up from super featherweight to face a champion who breaks opponents down through sustained volume carries enormous risk.

Top Rank must decide if the reward justifies taking that chance. Navarrete holds the IBF and WBO titles at 130 pounds, where a unification against WBC champion O’Shaquie Foster remains an attractive option.

Top Rank has another route into the lightweight picture. WBO champion Abdullah Mason sat ringside for Zepeda’s win over Roach and is already an obvious choice for a unification bout.

If Top Rank wants one of its champions in with Zepeda, Mason can take the fight without changing divisions. Sending Navarrete back to lightweight after his previous loss is the riskier move, especially against a relentless pressure fighter who would force him to work every minute.

Ghana News.title: Peace Council calls for stronger support for school peace education
Ghana News.content:
The National Peace Council (NPC)

The National Peace Council (NPC) has called for stronger stakeholder collaboration to deepen peace education in schools and sustain Ghana’s peace.

The Council said equipping young people with dialogue, tolerance, mutual respect and non-violence was critical to addressing emerging challenges, including misinformation, cyberbullying, hate speech, intolerance and substance abuse.

Madam Janet Sarney-Kuma, Director, Capacity Development and Outreach, NPC, made the call at a media briefing in Accra on the National Peace Council School Engagement Programme.

She said preventing conflicts helped keep schools open, while equipping learners with the values of dialogue and responsible citizenship enabled them to become lifelong ambassadors of peace.

Madam Sarney-Kuma said the programme sought to strengthen public understanding of peace education and collaboration with the media in highlighting young people’s contributions to peace in schools and communities.

She said schools were not only centres of academic learning but also places where character was formed, leadership nurtured and responsible citizenship developed.

“If Ghana is to sustain its hard-earned peace, we must intentionally cultivate the values of

dialogue, tolerance, respect and non-violence in our schools and classrooms,” she said.

Madam Sarney-Kuma said the Council worked with the Ghana Education Service, school authorities and other partners to promote peace education through classroom engagements, peace clubs, civic education, leadership mentoring and community outreach.

She said the programme had reached schools across all regions and empowered thousands of learners to serve as ambassadors of peace in their schools, homes and communities.

Madam Sarney-Kuma said peace education had become increasingly important because of young people’s exposure to misinformation, cyberbullying, hate speech and other social vices.

“Peace education is not a luxury. It is a necessity. It equips learners with the values and life skills to resolve differences peacefully, appreciate diversity and become responsible citizens,” she stated.

She said the programme was yielding positive results, with learners embracing dialogue rather than violence, promoting mutual respect through peace clubs and demonstrating leadership among their peers.

Madam Sarney-Kuma called on the Ghana Education Service, parents, teachers, faith-based organisations, traditional authorities, civil society organisations, development partners and the private sector to support peace education.

The Council also appealed to the media to give greater prominence to stories promoting peace and social cohesion.

“Conflict often dominates headlines, yet peace stories rarely receive the same attention. We invite you to help change this narrative by highlighting stories of young peace ambassadors in schools and promoting dialogue in communities where understanding is transforming lives,” she noted.

Madam Sarney-Kuma said the Council aspired to see every school become a centre for peace education and every learner become a champion of dialogue and national cohesion.

She urged stakeholders to continue working together to build a culture of peace, “one school, one student, one teacher and one community at a time.”

Ghana News.title: NDC’s future depends on youth wing – Armah Buah
Ghana News.content:
The Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, has stressed the need for the National Democratic Congress (NDC) to invest continuously in its youth wing to secure the party’s future.

He said young people formed a significant part of Ghana’s electorate and must therefore be equipped with the skills and leadership capacity required to contribute to both the party and national development.

Speaking at the opening of a two-day Western Regional Quadrennial Youth Conference of the NDC in Takoradi, Mr Armah-Kofi Buah urged young party members to remain committed, patient and hardworking while positioning themselves to take advantage of emerging opportunities.

“The NDC’s future is tied to the youth wing, and if we take our eye off the ball on the youth front, as a political party, we will not survive. If people have not checked the data, the last time I checked, over 70% of the voters in Ghana are under 40 years,” he said.

The Minister also said the government was working to expand opportunities for young people, indicating that the next national budget would place significant emphasis on youth empowerment.

He cited initiatives in education, healthcare and employment as part of efforts to restore confidence in the economy, while highlighting the creation of more than 2,000 jobs through the Blue Water Guards initiative under his ministry.

Addressing the youth, Mr Armah-Kofi Buah urged them to remain focused despite delays in securing opportunities, assuring them that commitment and hard work would eventually be recognised.

“I think as a youth front, one of the messages I want you to take is that in the NDC, the word is work hard, sacrifice, don’t even look back. But somebody is watching you, and you will be rewarded at the right time,” he said.

He further encouraged the youth to avoid undermining others in their pursuit of political advancement, stressing that dedication to the party and service to the country would create opportunities for them to assume leadership in the future.

Ghana News.title: James Agalga won’t tolerate attacks on his integrity – Political analyst
Ghana News.content:
Political analyst Dr Jonathan Asante Otchere has cautioned against attempts to question the integrity of newly appointed Majority Leader, James Agalga, saying his personality and experience could shape a firm approach to his new role.

Dr Asante Otchere said Mr Agalga, the Member of Parliament for Builsa North and former Deputy Minister for the Interior, was known for his calm demeanour but could be uncompromising when his integrity was challenged.

He said the new Majority Leader’s experience in government and Parliament would also be important as he takes charge of the Majority caucus.

Mr Agalga has assumed the leadership position following the appointment of former Majority Leader Mahama Ayariga as Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs-designate in President John Dramani Mahama’s latest ministerial reshuffle.

Speaking on Channel One TV on Saturday, August 8, Dr Asante Otchere said Mr Agalga was a “no-nonsense” personality who was unlikely to overlook attempts to impugn his character.

“The one taking over the Majority Leadership. And we all know that he’s also a smooth, slow talker like Mr. Ayariga. But he is more tough and a little bit no-nonsense person when he feels that you’re trying to indict his integrity, he will not pardon or forgive you,” he said.

Meanwhile, Mr Agalga has rejected suggestions that he could be intimidated by the demands of his new position, maintaining that his years of experience in Parliament have equipped him to lead the House effectively.

Ghana News.title: COPEC calls for strategic fuel reserve to cushion Ghana against price shocks
Ghana News.content:
The government should consider establishing a strategic petroleum reserve to shield consumers from sudden increases in fuel prices and possible disruptions to supplies, the Chamber of Petroleum Consumers (COPEC) has proposed.

The reserve, according to COPEC, would allow the state to purchase and store petroleum products when international prices are favourable and release them onto the market when prices rise sharply.

Such a mechanism, the organisation argued, would provide Ghana with a buffer against fluctuations on the international market and reduce the impact of sudden fuel price increases on consumers.

COPEC also proposed that part of the petroleum products processed by local refineries could be channelled into the reserve to gradually build up the country’s stock.

“If I decide to even release that stock at $600 or $700, as a government, I’ll be able to recoup the investment I put in, and I’ll be able to sustain fuel prices,” he said.

The proposal comes amid recent increases in petroleum prices, with diesel rising from about GH¢14 to GH¢16 per litre to nearly GH¢20 per litre within a relatively short period.

COPEC said the recent price movements highlight the need for Ghana to develop a long-term mechanism to manage international market volatility rather than relying mainly on interventions after prices have already risen.

It suggested that between five and 10 per cent of products processed by local refineries could be set aside to build the strategic stock.

“The refineries seem to be working now, but I would advocate again that 5%, 10% of what the refineries are processing now, put it in a strategic reserve buffer,” he said.

Speaking on Channel One TV on Saturday, August 8, the Executive Secretary of COPEC, Duncan Amoah, said the reserve could be deployed during periods of severe price increases or when international supply disruptions prevent fuel cargoes from reaching Ghana.

“Tomorrow when you wake up, and there’s a reason for which cargoes cannot come, or prices have jumped from $800 to about $2,000, you can fall on these buffers,” he said.

Mr Amoah welcomed the government’s recent decision to reduce the price of diesel by GH¢2 per litre but said such measures should complement, rather than replace, a long-term strategy for managing fuel price volatility.

Ghana News.title: Kristo Asafo Mission reaffirms Nana Kwadwo Safo Akofena I as new leader
Ghana News.content:
The Kristo Asafo Mission of Ghana has reaffirmed Nana Kwadwo Safo Akofena I as the new leader of the church following the death of its founder, Apostle Emeritus Dr Kwadwo Safo Kantanka.

The Mission said his selection was carried out by the council of elders in line with the succession arrangement left by the late founder.

The reaffirmation was made during a National Joint Intercessory Prayer Service held to honour Apostle Emeritus Dr Kwadwo Safo Kantanka as part of activities marking his birth month.

The service, held under the theme “Intercessory Prayer to Mark the Birth Month of Our Founder As He Rests in His Glory”, brought together members of the Mission to remember the founder and pray for the continued progress of the church.

The Mission explained that the founder had provided guidance on who should take over the leadership of the church in the event of his death.

According to the arrangement, the council was required to select one of his three sons to lead the Mission.

Speaking at the prayer service, the Public Relations Officer of the Kristo Asafo Mission of Ghana, Akwesi Ofori, said the council carefully considered the succession process before settling on Nana Kwadwo Safo Akofena I.

“When you look into the books, the founder mentioned that when he is not around, the council of the church should select any of his three sons to be the leader of the church,” he said.

Mr Ofori said the decision was reached after careful deliberations, acknowledging that choosing a new leader was not an easy task for the council.

“I think the council did very well. Selecting the new leader was not an easy task for the council. But with good counsel, they were able to come out with Nana Kwadwo Safo Akofena I,” he said.

He urged members of the Mission to rally behind the new leader and support his vision for the continued growth of the church.

“We are gathered here with our new leader, and he is the one we must listen to and follow through with his vision for the church,” Mr Ofori said.

Ghana News.title: Prosecuting politicians does not mean Ghana’s democracy is under attack – Duncan Amoah to NPP
Ghana News.content:
The Executive Secretary of the Chamber of Petroleum Consumers (COPEC), Duncan Amoah, has dismissed claims that investigations involving politicians and public officials amount to an attack on Ghana’s democracy.

He said the scrutiny of former government officials should not automatically be interpreted as political persecution, arguing that accountability remains an important part of a functioning democratic system.

His comments come after the New Patriotic Party’s “Democracy Under Attack” demonstration on August 6, 2026, during which the party raised concerns over alleged threats to democratic governance and what it described as the targeting of its members.

Mr Amoah said Ghana’s democratic institutions must be allowed to perform their duties, while citizens retain the right to question or criticise the manner in which those institutions operate.

“When you have institutions get to work, you don’t have any objection but to sometimes critique the way institutions work. But to lump everything together and say the entire democratic process is under attack, some of us would beg to differ,” he said.

He also said he was yet to see a situation in Ghana where an opposition figure was targeted simply for openly expressing political views.

“I have not in Ghana seen or come across an opposition element being just vocal and being targeted by government,” he said.

Mr Amoah further pointed to freedom of expression as evidence that Ghana’s democratic space remains open, stressing that citizens continue to have the opportunity to voice their opinions on national issues.

“Freedom of speech, which is one of the core tenets of democracy, clearly is also not being attacked as we speak. You can speak your mind,” he said.

Speaking on Channel One TV on Saturday, August 8, Mr Amoah, however, cautioned political actors against crossing the line from legitimate criticism into threats or intimidation.

He said political discourse should allow room for robust criticism while ensuring that statements made by political actors do not threaten individuals or undermine the rule of law.

Ghana News.title: Duncan Amoah cautions against political threats in Ghana’s democracy
Ghana News.content:
The Executive Secretary of the Chamber of Petroleum Consumers (COPEC), Duncan Amoah, has cautioned political actors against using veiled threats in Ghana’s political discourse, warning that such rhetoric could undermine democratic accountability.

He said suggestions that political opponents would face retaliation when there is a change in government could discourage legitimate investigations and create a culture where public officials fear accountability.

The comments follow the New Patriotic Party’s “Democracy Under Attack” demonstration on August 6, 2026, during which the party raised concerns about alleged political persecution and threats to democratic governance.

Duncan Amoah, however, disagreed with the suggestion that Ghana’s democracy was currently under attack, arguing that citizens and political parties continued to have the space to express their views and challenge government decisions.

“My personal view is no,” he said when asked whether democracy was under attack in Ghana.

He however, expressed concern about what he described as an increasing use of subtle threats in political conversations, particularly statements suggesting that those currently in power could face reprisals when the political tide changes.

“What is concerning is the growing tendency for subtle threats to enter our political discourse. You see a threat from the opposition that says the tables will turn and we will do things to you. You hear functionaries sometimes issue those threats,” he said.

He said such comments could create the impression that investigations into alleged wrongdoing should be halted because those being scrutinised could eventually return to power.

“What you are indirectly saying is that even if we did wrong, or adverse findings are made against us, do not go after us because someday you may not be in power,” he stated.

Speaking on Citi FM on Saturday, August 8, Mr Amoah said political interests should not be allowed to take precedence over accountability, stressing that the consequences would ultimately be borne by the wider population.

“If we allow this country to be governed that way, it is not the NPP or NDC that suffers; it is the people,” he said.

Ghana News.title: Ghana High Commission to proceed with PhD students’ verification and oath-taking
Ghana News.content:
Ghana’s High Commissioner to the United Kingdom, Sabah Zita Benson

Ghana’s High Commissioner to the United Kingdom, Sabah Zita Benson, has confirmed that the High Commission will proceed with a planned verification and oath-taking exercise for PhD students in the UK sponsored by the Ghana Scholarships Authority (GSA).

The exercise has attracted opposition from representatives of the scholarship beneficiaries, who have described the requirement as discriminatory and unnecessary, arguing that they had already signed bonds committing them to return to Ghana after completing their studies.

The students’ leadership, in a statement issued on Friday, August 7, questioned the basis for introducing an additional oath-taking requirement and raised concerns over outstanding tuition and stipend payments.

Madam Benson, however, said the students’ scholarship bonds already contained provisions requiring beneficiaries to comply with conditions set by the GSA, including surveys and evaluations.

She also pointed to a clause requiring beneficiaries to return to Ghana within two months of completing their studies, adding that those who fail to honour their obligations could be required to refund the scholarship funds received.

The High Commissioner further rejected demands by the students for guaranteed reintegration into Ghana’s job market, arguing that no such commitment was contained in the scholarship agreements they signed.

“In the bond they signed, I see no obligation by Government to reintegrate them into society,” she said.

She questioned why some of the concerns being raised by the students were not brought up earlier, particularly as the beneficiaries were awarded scholarships between 2020 and 2025.

Madam Benson also dismissed claims that the oath-taking requirement was being applied retrospectively, maintaining that the GSA had the authority to introduce measures necessary to ensure compliance with scholarship conditions.

“The Ghana High Commission, acting on behalf of the GSA, shall go ahead with the planned verification and oath-taking,” she stated.

She said the exercise was being undertaken in the interest of taxpayers and to ensure that beneficiaries fulfil the obligations attached to the scholarships, adding that the government had reasons for introducing the verification process.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
