World.title: Citizens of nowhere: G.B. Road’s sex workers at risk of exclusion in ongoing SIR
World.content:
The ongoing special intensive revision (SIR) of voter rolls in Delhi has cast an ominous shadow over women sex workers in Garstin Bastion (G.B.) Road brothels. Many of them don’t possess the documents listed by the Election Commission (EC) to verify their details or an extract of the previous SIR with their names or those of a blood relative for mapping, given that they were trafficked to the brothels at an age when they were too young to remember their place of birth.

With the fear of losing their vote has come another fear — that they would be asked to leave. But where? No one can tell. For many who have spent decades on G.B. Road shifting between brothels, the uncertainty over what exclusion from the SIR might mean is growing by the day.

One sex worker, Rita*, in her 40s, told The Hindu that she had exercised her franchise in every election since the 2010 Delhi Assembly poll. “It made me feel equal in some sense. Life is already challenging for us,” she said.

Marked ‘shifted’

A large section of G.B. Road’s 2,800 sex workers, who live in cramped lanes with limited access to basic amenities, is 40 or older, and only 650 of them are on the electoral roll.

A Booth Level Officer (BLO) said she has marked 783 voters ‘shifted’ in her booth, which has more than 1,300 voters. Of those marked ‘shifted’, 450 are sex workers.

None of the 14 women interviewed for this story were in touch with their family, making it impossible to check their details in the previous SIR. They have never been enrolled in school and only possess Aadhaar, PAN and Voter IDs as identity proofs.

However, these documents are not included in the EC’s list of acceptable verification documents if an elector is not linked to the previous SIR in the enumeration phase. As per the commission, the motto of the exercise is to “ensure that no eligible voter is left out, while no ineligible voter is included in the roll.”

‘Will we have to leave?’

Basanti*, who has been a sex worker for more than 30 years, was only 12 when she was allegedly trafficked from Bengaluru (then Bangalore) to G.B. Road. Though she knows little about the SIR exercise, she said her form was filled out, but she didn’t receive any acknowledgement slip.

On hearing about the outcome of the exercise, she echoed the concern of many in her position. “So, if I don’t have a birth certificate or if I never took a matric exam, I cannot vote? Will we be asked to leave Delhi?” she said.

At 52, she has been in rehabilitation for the past four years and has stopped sex work. “I have spent all my life here. I only remember my father’s name. I don’t even know if he is alive or dead.”

No valid certificate

Among the 100 returned forms, the BLO said fewer than five electors had been mapped in the previous SIR.

“The names of those who return the form will be published in the draft roll. If mapping hasn’t been done, they will receive notice to submit any of the 12 documents listed by the EC. However, most of these women don’t have any of those documents, such as a birth certificate, a Class 10 or 12 school certificate, or a permanent residence ownership document. Their names will likely get removed,” the BLO said, adding that nearly 100 more forms are yet to be returned.

Sunita, a social worker associated with Kat-Katha NGO, said that most sex workers were trafficked to the area as teenagers, losing contact with their families. “Access to all women here is also very restricted. It depends on whom they are working for,” she said.

She added that marking sex workers as ‘shifted’ is wrong.

“They switch brothels, which means changing floor, building or a different room. But they are not moving out of the area. It is very common here. The BLO should know that,” she said.

‘Process discriminatory’

Safrin*, in her 30s, who moved to Delhi from Meerut eight years ago, said she voted for the first time in the 2024 general election. “All of us are at the mercy of landlords and NGOs to help us,” she said.

Ms. Safrin said the SIR exercise does not acknowledge them.

“Sex work is helping me raise my children after the death of my husband and save for my daughters’ marriages. But the government doesn’t acknowledge us. If they did, they would know that a sex worker cannot provide family documents. I don’t even remember my mother’s name, so where will I get the birth certificate from?”

Rita*, in her 40s, who stays in a room beside Ms. Safrin, said the migrant working class drives a city but is treated with indifference. “Our rights as citizens are already limited. This exercise is discriminatory. If at this age, you want me to prove that I am Indian or take away my right to choose my Chief Minister or Prime Minister, then take it. What will we be able to do anyway?”

Children of some sex workers, such as Ms. Rita’s son Ravi, are hopeful that their 10th- and 12th-grade certificates will help in the enrolment process.

Speaking to The Hindu, Joint Chief Electoral Officer Balram Meena said there is no separate process for marginalised groups such as the homeless and sex workers. “If their mapping can’t be done and there are no documents either, their names will be removed as per the process.”

(*Names changed on request)

World.title: New criminal laws introduced to provide speedy justice to citizens: Union Home Minister Amit Shah
World.content:
The Union Government’s decision to replace the colonial-era laws with the three criminal laws — the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam — was aimed to provide justice to citizens through a system that was more technology driven and time bound, said Union Home Minister Amit Shah in Puducherry on Sunday (August 9, 2026).

Participating in the presentation ceremony of the President’s Police Colour to the Puducherry Police at a parade held at the Police Training School ground in Gorimedu, the Home Minister said the new criminal laws are aimed to provide speedy justice to citizens of India.

“The new laws are based on three pillars of technology, timeline and trust. The aim was to provide justice to the people of our country,” Mr. Shah said.

Lauding the Puducherry Police for bagging the prestigious President’s Police Colour, he said “receiving the award is a glorious moment for any disciplined police force. It is a force with a strength of less than 5,000 personnel entrusted with the task of maintaining internal security. During COVID-19 pandemic, while reviewing the situation in Union Territories, I got an opportunity to experience the good work of Puducherry police. They did a good job in a difficult situation,” he said.

Promising the Union Territory administration full support in initiating welfare and development works, Mr. Shah said the Centre has provided around ₹ 13,762 crore between 2014 and 2026. Around 7.7 lakh people of Puducherry have benefitted from Central schemes including Jal Jeevan Mission, Ayushman Bharat, Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana and Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi.

Earlier, the Minister handed over a ceremonial colour flag to the Puducherry Police at a parade marking the conferment of the President’s Police Colour. Before handing over the flag, Superintendents of Police Subham Sundar Ghosh and Rachna Singh led a Pile-the-Drum Ceremony as part of handing over the flag. The Puducherry Police become the 18th State/Union Territory in the country to be bestowed with the highest honour conferred upon police force in the country.

Mr. Shah also presented the Kendriya Griha Mantri Dakshata Padak and scrolls to Senior Superintendent of Police R. Kalaivanan and Senior Superintendent of Police Lakshmi Soujanya. Lieutenant Governor K. Kailashnathan, Chief Minister N. Rangasamy, Home Minister A. Namassivayam and Director General of Police Shalini Singh spoke at the event. Ministers, legislators belonging to the ruling AINRC, BJP and senior officers attended the event.

World.title: Pentagon pushes defence companies to boost weapons production after concerns of depleted stocks
World.content:
The Pentagon is pressing the U.S. defence industry to accelerate production of weapons to help replenish its diminished stockpile of munitions, including those depleted in the ongoing war with Iran.

Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said in a statement on Saturday (August 8, 2026) that the department was actively focused on boosting munitions acquisitions to provide “the weapons our warfighters need at the pace the threat demands.” He confirmed department efforts in the last week to significantly speed the process but insisted it was part of a broader modernisation effort that predated the five-month-old conflict.

Deputy Defence Secretary Steve Feinberg wrote to industry leaders on Wednesday, giving them no more than 21 days to submit plans to “drive significantly faster, more aggressive delivery schedules and/or increased production for critical capabilities," according to a memo obtained by The Washington Post.

“Years-long development cycles are not acceptable,” Mr. Feinberg wrote. “We must dramatically accelerate our program schedules and expand our production capacity now.” The memo comes as recent fighting with Iran used up more of the U.S. military's already diminished stockpiles of advanced missile interceptors, potentially putting American troops at more risk if hostilities resume, according to a new analysis.

Shrunken inventories of Patriot and THAAD interceptors may force the U.S. and its West Asian allies to take more risks to conserve those air defences, according to the analysis from the Centre for Strategic and International Studies, a Washington think tank. For example, it said, American forces may launch fewer missiles against incoming Iranian drones and missiles, raising the chance of one getting through.

President Donald Trump in recent days has bristled over public reports of a munitions shortage, posting on Truth Social on Thursday that the U.S. has “massive amounts." He added that “large amounts are being manufactured and shipped to the U.S. as needed.” On Saturday (August 8), Mr. Parnell affirmed that Mr. Feinberg's memo seeking a rapid escalation of weapons production is “real," adding that it “will inform the fiscal year 2028 budget submitted to Congress for funding, and it is entirely consistent with our ongoing push to rebuild the defense industrial base.” A defence spending Bill is currently stalled in Congress, with lawmakers fuming over Mr. Trump's military action against Iran and resisting the White House request to substantially increase Pentagon spending to $1.5 trillion, up from about $900 billion last year.

The number of Patriot interceptors fell from 2,330 before the war to 1,030 when the April ceasefire took effect, CSIS estimated last month. Following recent fighting, the stockpile is now estimated to be between 759 and 827, a decrease of at least 65% since before the conflict began.

The number of THAAD interceptors fell from 452 before the war to between 232 and 262 at the start of the April ceasefire, CSIS said. The U.S. was able to replenish some of the inventory to between 234 and 278 interceptors. But the stockpile is still at least 38% smaller than it was before the conflict.

World.title: Those who participated in Quit India movement remain inspiration for every Indian: PM Modi
World.content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday (August 9, 2026) remembered those who participated in the historic Quit India Movement, and said their courage will always remain an inspiration for every Indian.

The Quit India Movement was launched under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi on August 9, 1942 and gave a decisive impetus to India's quest for independence.

"Remembering all those who participated in the historic Quit India Movement. Their courage will always remain an inspiration for every Indian," Mr. Modi said in a post on X.

Remembering all those who participated in the historic Quit India Movement. Their courage will always remain an inspiration for every Indian. Inspired by the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi Ji, the clarion call of Quit India infused new energy into our freedom struggle and reflected… — Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) August 9, 2026

The Prime Minister said the clarion call of Quit India infused new energy in the freedom struggle and reflected the unwavering determination of people to break free from colonial rule.

August 9, 2026, marks the 84th anniversary of the Quit India Movement, one of the defining milestones in the nation's freedom struggle.

World.title: Jharkhand exam stir: Government to hold fresh talks; health of student leader on fast deteriorates
World.content:
The Jharkhand government will hold fresh talks on Sunday (August 9, 2026) with aspirants protesting alleged recruitment exam irregularities for the 16th day now, a move a prominent student faction termed "political manoeuvring".

Also Read : Jharkhand students protest LIVE

The decision for another round of talks was taken after a series of meetings between the government and student groups on Friday (August 7, 2026) night and throughout Saturday (August 8, 2026) failed to break the deadlock.

Meanwhile, the condition of student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who has been on indefinite hunger strike for around a week now at Ranchi's Jaipal Singh Stadium, suddenly deteriorated around 3 a.m. Doctors recorded his blood glucose level at 53.

The Hemant Soren government on Friday (August 7, 2026) night held discussions with the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch that has been spearheading the agitation.

Then, throughout Saturday (August 8, 2026), it held four rounds of talks with different student groups, including the Congress' student wing NSUI, Jharkhand Chhatra Morcha (JCM) and Adivasi Chhatra Sangh (ACS).

However, since the meetings remained inconclusive, the government decided to hold a sixth round of talks with student representatives around 12 p.m. on Sunday (August 9, 2026).

The backlash was immediate.

The JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch accused the Jharkhand government of "political manoeuvring" by announcing another round of talks with student organisations, alleging the move was aimed at creating divisions among protesting students and diverting people's attention from their core demands.

Ravindra Paswan, a leader of the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, claimed the government was attempting to weaken the agitation by holding discussions with organisations that had "played no role in the ongoing protest".

"This is political manoeuvring by the government. It is trying to create a divide among students and divert attention. But they should know that all students are united," Mr. Paswan said at a press conference at the Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, where students have been protesting since July 25.

Paswan claimed the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch had placed all its demands before the five-member government panel during a detailed meeting on Friday night.

However, on Saturday (August 8, 2026), the panel, comprising Ministers Dipika Pandey Singh, Sudivya Kumar, Chamra Linda and Sanjay Prasad Yadav, held separate meetings with student bodies including the Congress-backed NSUI, JCM and Adivasi Chhatra Sangh ACS, and sought their respective charters of demands.

The government, however, said the discussions were held in a positive atmosphere and that it was considering the concerns raised by the protesting aspirants.

The decision for another round of talks was taken after a four-hour meeting between the government panel and Chief Minister Hemant Soren on Saturday (August 8, 2026) evening.

Rural Development Minister Dipika Pandey Singh said the panel had apprised the Chief Minister of the demands and concerns raised by student delegations during the discussions. "It was decided in the meeting with the Chief Minister that a final round of talks with the protesting students will take place at 12 p.m. on Sunday [August 9, 2026]," she said.

Minister Sanjay Prasad Yadav said the government would continue discussions with the agitators demanding comprehensive reforms in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).

The JCM submitted five demands, including cancellation of the 14th JPSC Civil Services Examination, while the NSUI submitted six demands, including a CID probe into all JPSC and JSSC examinations under suspicion within 90 days and the establishment of a Jharkhand Testing Agency on the lines of the National Testing Agency.

ACS leader Kartik Oraon demanded inclusion of tribal and regional languages as qualifying papers in recruitment examinations and cancellation of tests in which irregularities were found.

Higher and Technical Education Minister Sudivya Kumar said the government had issued an email ID to seek suggestions from aspirants on reforms in the recruitment process.

Despite the talks, the protesters have maintained that their agitation will continue until all their demands are fulfilled. They have also announced a march to the Assembly on August 10 if the government fails to meet their demands by Sunday (August 9, 2026)

Meanwhile, the All India Students' Association (AISA) set up a separate platform at the stadium on Saturday (August 8, 2026), but its leaders said the move should not be seen as a separate agitation.

AISA national president Neha Bora, who was attacked with ink during Friday's (August 7, 2026) Assembly march near Birsa Chowk, briefly joined the protest and raised slogans demanding cancellation of the 14th JPSC and JSSC-CGL examinations.

The outfit's Ranchi unit chief Vijay Kumar said the organisation had the same demands as the larger agitation and that its members would participate in the August 10 march without carrying the AISA banner.

The agitation has also witnessed protests by the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP), whose members on Friday (August 7, 2026) scuffled with police while attempting to break through barricades near the chief minister's residence.

Around eight to 10 ABVP protesters were detained during the march but were subsequently released, Deputy Superintendent of Police (Headquarters) Ajay Aryan said.

The ABVP has announced a separate Vidhan Sabha march on August 11.

Nineteen people have so far been arrested in connection with alleged irregularities in JPSC examinations, while former panel chairperson L. Khiangte has been questioned four times since July 28.

World.title: YSRCP leaders condemn arrest of Amadalavalasa in-charge in Ampolu case
World.content:
Several senior leaders of the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP), including former Ministers Dharmana Prasada Rao and Dharmana Krishna Das and MLC Kumbha Ravibabu, strongly condemned the arrest of the party’s Amadalavalasa constituency in-charge Chintada Ravikumar on Saturday (August 8, 2026) night on the outskirts of Srikakulam.

The police arrested Mr. Ravikumar and 25 others on charges of misbehaviour with a woman Sub-Inspector during former Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy’s visit on July 30, 2026 to Ampolu to console former Minister Seediri Appalaraju, who had been arrested in an accident case involving his son.

In a press release, Mr. Prasada Rao alleged that the State government had misused the police for political vendetta against YSRCP leaders in Srikakulam and other parts of the State.

He alleged that a heated argument with the police during Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy’s visit had been made a pretext to arrest Mr. Ravikumar in the case. He said video footage clearly showed that Mr. Ravikumar had not misbehaved with anyone during the visit.

Mr. Ravibabu asked the government to withdraw all cases filed against the YSRCP leaders, saying they had not crossed their limits. The party staged protests in Amadalavalasa and other places over the arrests. Family members of some of the accused claimed that many of them were not in town on July 30, 2026, but their names were included in the First Information Report intentionally.

World.title: Two sisters killed after being hit by bike in Thiruvananthapuram
World.content:
Two sisters were killed after a motorcycle struck them while they were crossing the National Highway 66 (NH 66) bypass road in Thiruvananthapuram on Sunday (August 9, 2026).

The deceased have been identified as Shanthamma (62), and Vijayamm (70), who hailed from Thiruvallam. The incident occurred around 7 a.m. at the at Karimbuvila junction near Thiruvallam.

The sisters were reportedly on their way to a temple in Nagercoil when the accident occurred.

According to preliminary information, the two women were crossing the bypass from the service road. They were holding hands and crossing the road when a motorcycle approaching from the opposite direction hit them and threw them onto the road.

Despite being rushed to a nearby hospital by passersby and local residents, the sisters succumbed to their injuries.

The City police have commenced a hunt to apprehend the motorcyclist and assess the circumstances of the mishap, including the speed of the vehicle. (EOM)

World.title: Egypt could join Pak-Saudi-Turkiye defence pact once technical issues resolved, says Turkish foreign minister
World.content:
Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on Saturday he believed Egypt could join a defence pact signed between Turkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia once several technical issues were resolved.

“Egypt is already our natural partner on all issues. I believe that at the next stage, Egypt will also be among us in the alliance. We already act toward one another as if we were alliance members. There are a few technical issues. Once these are implemented, there is no reason for Egypt not to be part of it,” he told Turkiye’s state-run Anadolu news agency.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, signed in the Saudi city on Friday, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empowers the three states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

Fidan said other countries had expressed interest in joining the agreement, but the founding members had debated how the expansion should be handled.

Some countries that wanted to join asked not to be named, he said, adding that the preferred model was for Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan to remain the three core founding countries, responsible for establishing the principles, standards and long-term structure of the alliance, while other countries could join with the approval of the core members.

“Under our president’s vision, we should not remain limited to three countries. We should grow,” Fidan said.

Fidan also said the initiative was broader than the traditional definition of the Middle East because of Pakistan’s participation.

Pakistan’s geographical position meant the initiative went beyond the conventional definition of the Middle East and represented a broader regional perspective.

‘Same as Nato’s Article 5’

Fidan further elaborated on this, saying the pact was technically the same as Nato’s Article 5 mutual defence agreement.

Article 5 of the North Atlantic alliance specifies that an attack on one ​of its members is an attack on all of them. It obliges allies to take action they deem necessary to assist the country under attack, including potentially the use of military force.

While the Makkah defence pact stipulates the same, Fidan explained that its text contained general commitments whose practical implementation would depend on discussions and decisions by relevant bodies.

A country would need to make a request for assistance and would determine the type of support it needs, he said, adding that the requests could be of different kinds, ranging from intelligence and logistics to ammunition or, if necessary, military units, depending on the scale of the threat.

The signatories, he said, would decide through consultations what degree, form, and format of ​support they would ask for in the event of an attack, but that no country would be considered a ​threat as long as a member state is not attacked.

Fidan also said that the new alliance was not directed against Iran or any other country, but rather served as a general pledge to support the three signatories’ security.

He further told Anadolu that discussions on the initiative began before the current war environment, when there was no US-Israel war on Iran and other regional countries had also been involved in the talks leading to the agreement.

Fidan said its signatories were countries that did not have expansionist policies. “They are countries concerned with their own borders, their own problems and their development, and, if possible, they want to contribute positively to their environment through good relations and good neighborliness.“

The three countries, he said, had different styles and capacities, but when brought together, they naturally formed a defence-oriented organisation rather than an offensive one.

“It is not an approach of going on the offensive and saying, ‘Let’s do this or that together.’ Therefore, unless it is attacked by a country, whether from inside or outside the region, this alliance cannot have any dispute with any country. But, of course, the power composition we have put forward will make a constructive contribution to regional stability,” he said.

He termed the pact the “most important step” toward bringing lasting stability to this region.

How will the alliance function?

According to Fidan, the pact would be operational under a political and military committee comprising foreign and defence ministers and chiefs of general staff, similar to Nato structures.

The committee would translate the vision set by the leaders into decisions and carry out related work, while a secretariat would be established to implement those decisions, he explained.

“At the first committee meeting, ministers would likely present proposals to the leaders on the establishment, structure and functioning of the secretariat, as well as its initial tasks,” he said, adding that the pact would cover a broad range of military issues, including interoperability, or the ability of countries with different military structures to operate together. Other areas would include joint training, mutual support, logistics, threat assessments, intelligence sharing and, most importantly, defence industry cooperation.

He said the committee would meet at certain intervals during the year and that a permanent secretariat would be established in Saudi Arabia. The structure, functioning and additional units of the secretariat would be determined in discussions among the members.

Fidan added that joint exercises and training would be necessary to establish the ability of the countries to operate together.

“Because after a while you will see that when you find yourselves in a common combat scenario, how your weapons systems and communications systems will communicate with one another and how they will be compatible are important issues. These are the things that will be done after the secretariat is established,” he said.

He said standards would need to be developed and that analyses and assessments would also be carried out.

‘Support in the Muslim world and the West’

Fidan said the defence agreement had received strong support from countries in the Muslim world, including those that were not members but were nevertheless very pleased with the agreement.

He said there were also supporters in the West who understood the substance of the initiative.

“Especially in the Islamic world, there are many who strongly support this issue. There are also supporters in the West, among those who understand the essence of the matter. The way for the Middle East to cease being a place that produces problems for humanity and the international community and instead become a place that creates added value with everything it possesses is through implementing constructive alliances of this kind,” Fidan said.

Fidan said the leadership of Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan had created significant regional and global expectations and that officials now had the responsibility to fill those expectations professionally.

“Our responsibility, in the positions we hold, is to recognise that the political will put forward by the leadership of the three countries has created a very significant regional and global expectation. We need to fill that expectation very professionally, move forward step by step and make it work. We have begun doing this, and God willing, we will continue,” he said.

World.title: On-duty cop martyred, another injured in Lakki Marwat attack
World.content:
LAKKI MARWAT: A constable was martyred and another sustained bullet wounds while on duty in an attack in the Saeedkhel area of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Lakki Marwat district on Sunday, police said.

District police officer’s spokesperson Qudratullah Khan told Dawn that the cops were attacked near the Saeedkhel graveyard, in the limits of the City Police Station.

“The terrorists opened fire on the rider squad personnel while they were patrolling the area,” he said, adding that Constable Sajidullah lost his life in the attack while Constable Muhammad Waqas was seriously wounded.

The body of the deceased constable and the injured policeman were taken to the Government City Hospital, he said.

Meanwhile, a large police contingent reached the site of the attack, surrounded the area and launched a search for the assailants, he said.

Security personnel and law enforcers have been coming under attack in KP, which continues to face terrorism.

According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies’ (PICSS) monthly security assessment released on July 31, security personnel deaths in terrorism incidents in KP, excluding merged districts, increased from 12 in June to 38 in July and terrorist deaths from 37 to 108, reflecting a rise by 192pc. But civilian deaths fell from 26 to seven, a decline by 73pc. One peace committee member was also killed.

Security personnel deaths in merged districts rose from six to 11 and terrorist deaths fell from 72 to 55. Civilian deaths, meanwhile, rose by 86pc, increasing from seven to 13.

World.title: Goods, oil transporters’ strike threatens industry, exports
World.content:
KARACHI: Goods carriers remain parked in Mauripur on Saturday, disrupting cargo movement to and from the city’s ports.—Online

• Movement of over 400,000 goods-carrying vehicles suspended

• Transporters refuse to end strike before talks with govt

KARACHI: A countrywide strike by goods transporters and oil tankers started affecting industrial and export supply chains on Saturday, with operators vowing to continue the protest until the outcome of talks with the government on Monday, while manufacturers warned that prolonged disruption could halt production and jeopardise export commitments.

Pakistan Goods Transporters Alliance Chairman Nisar Hussain Jafry told Dawn that “our countrywide strike will continue as our leadership intends to meet the ministers concerned with petroleum, transport and ports on Monday”.

He said the movement of more than 400,000 goods-carrying vehicles, ranging from small to large, had been suspended from Saturday until the outcome of Monday’s meeting. “We have already unloaded our containers at the ports,” he said.

Mr Jafry said goods transporters were striking over multiple issues, including the government’s recently introduced daily fuel price mechanism.

“We are dissatisfied with the daily fuel price fixation introduced by the government, which is only creating problems,” he said.

Since intercity movement of vehicles takes between one and three days, transporters and industries cannot make firm commitments on transportation charges because of daily changes in fuel prices, he said.

Mr Jafry urged the government to restore the monthly fuel price mechanism and reduce withholding tax on transporters to 2pc from 7pc, noting that oil carriers were paying 2pc withholding tax on services.

He said the government and goods transporters had signed a charter of demands in December 2025, but the commitments made under it had yet to be fulfilled.

Mr Jafry also complained about the number of toll plazas, saying they had been established at intervals of around 30km and that transporters were perturbed over high toll rates.

Transporters were also facing issues related to parking of heavy vehicles in areas surrounding the ports and driving licences, he added.

Supply-chain disruption

Already struggling with high production costs, industrialists warned that the nationwide strike by goods transporters could further disrupt industrial activity if supplies of raw materials remained suspended.

They cautioned that prolonged disruption in cargo movement could paralyse factories, derail production schedules and jeopardise export commitments, ultimately affecting employment and the overall economy.

SITE Association of Industry President Abdul Rehman Fudda said the strike had created an alarming situation for manufacturers.

“The entire production system depends on timely supply of raw materials and delivery of finished goods. If factories fail to receive essential inputs, production will stall, while delays in dispatching finished products will worsen financial stress for industries,” he said.

The export sector was already grappling with multiple challenges, Mr Fudda said, warning that if export consignments failed to reach buyers on time because of the transporters’ strike, industries could face penalties, price cuts or claims for damages.

He urged the government to intervene urgently and resolve the dispute through negotiations with goods transporters.

“Authorities must act before the situation escalates to the point where the country’s industry and supply chain collapse entirely. If the strike prolongs, the damage will extend beyond manufacturers — affecting exports, jobs and overall economic activity,” he said.

Mr Fudda also called for immediate relief measures for the industrial sector, warning that rising production costs, expensive energy and policy uncertainty were putting the survival of industries at serious risk.

He said escalating electricity and gas tariffs, rising production costs, high financing expenses and the absence of consistent economic policies had significantly undermined industrial activity.

Despite these challenges, he said, the business community continued to keep the wheels of the economy moving, adding that further neglect of the industrial sector would be against the country’s economic interests.

He called on the government to ensure energy supplies at competitive tariffs, simplify the tax regime, expedite payment of pending refunds, improve the ease of doing business and introduce investor-friendly policies.

Published in Dawn, August 9th, 2026

World.title: Fuel cost hits Lahore Metro service
World.content:
• Private firm says bus operations to be suspended from 11th as talks with authorities fail

• Punjab Mass Transit Authority calls move ‘blackmail’, vows to challenge court order against it

LAHORE: A private firm operating the Lahore Metro Bus on the 27km Gajjumata-Shahdra route has decided to suspend its operations from Aug 11 after talks with the Punjab Mass Transit Authority (PMA) over rising fuel costs and other issues failed to yield a solution.

As the company has served a final notice on the PMA, the authority has termed the move an attempt to blackmail and pressure the government into accepting its demands. It said it would challenge the court verdict against it and invoke a clause in the contract that provides for the appointment of arbitrators by both parties to settle any dispute.

According to the final notice, the company referred to its letters of July 31 and Aug 4, which had yet to be responded to by the PMA, and a meeting held on Aug 6 between company representatives and authority officials regarding implementation of the court’s July 29 orders directing the PMA to provide fuel from its own sources.

The company further said that during the meeting, it reiterated that it had exhausted its financial resources and was no longer in a position to continue operations.

On the occasion, the PMA stated that it was unable to take any decision without directions from the government.

The meeting concluded with an understanding that the PMA would propose a solution. However, the company said no solution or arrangement was communicated by the PMA.

It said that unless the PMA immediately commenced the uninterrupted supply of fuel from its own sources in compliance with the court orders, the metro bus operation could not be continued and would stand suspended from Aug 11.

“Any such suspension shall solely arise from PMA’s failure to implement the court order and shall not constitute any fault, default or unwillingness on the part of the company. All resulting operational, financial and legal consequences shall rest entirely with PMA,” the letter warned.

Talking to Dawn, a senior official of the company said the situation had worsened following frequent increases in fuel prices.

“When we took over, the diesel price was around Rs105 per litre or so. Later, the prices continued to rise from time to time, making it difficult for the company to meet its fuel costs,” the official added.

“In fact, the formula regarding calculation of fuel cost never reimbursed the company’s full fuel bill, as it covered only a fixed portion of the cost and the gap widened as soon as prices rose. When diesel prices increased sharply, the PMA’s payment increased slightly, but the company’s actual fuel expense increased much more,” the official, requesting anonymity, explained.

“A new formula was devised that reduced this gap but did not eliminate it, forcing the company to pay the remaining fuel costs from its own funds and borrowings, resulting in continuous losses and additional costs.”

To a question, he said the court in its orders of June 8, 2023 had directed the PMA to provide from its own sources. However, the PMA claimed the orders were already set aside by the respective court.

“For this, we sought clarification from the court as to whether or not the June 8, 2023 order had been cancelled. To this, the court issued a clarification on July 29, stating that the order had not been set aside and, therefore, the PMA should implement it, failing which action may be taken,” he maintained.

When contacted, a senior PMA official confirmed the court verdict against the authority.

“But we have already challenged this order in the relevant court. We are also invoking the contractual provision for appointing an arbitrator to decide the case,” he said, claiming that under the contract the company was being paid on a per-kilometre basis.

“We also raised the price. But the company is insisting on a further increase, which we cannot make without getting the government’s nod,” he added.

To a query, the official admitted that the PMA was not in a position to implement the court orders until it received approval from the government.

“We admit that fuel prices have increased. But we are unable to provide fuel to the company from our own sources as directed by the court. For this, the government [transport department] is the authority to do something,” the official added.

He said the PMA had some options to continue the metro bus service even if the company walked out of the system. “Though there could be some issues from Aug 11 onwards, we have managed to arrange some buses from outside in a bid to continue the service,” he added.

It is pertinent to mention that the Lahore Metro Bus Service, the country’s first modern mass transit project, was officially inaugurated and opened to the public on Feb 10-11, 2013, running on a 27-km route from Gajjumata to Shahdara.

World.title: Pakistan's Muhammad Zubair becomes Tekken 8 champion at Esports World Cup in Paris
World.content:
Pakistan’s Muhammad Zubair emerged victorious in the Tekken 8 championship at the Esports World Cup (EWC) in Paris on Saturday, becoming the new World Champion of the popular fighting game.

Zubair achieved a clean victory over South Korea’s LowHigh in the grand final of the tournament held from Aug 5-8, after having just scraped through during the early stages.

“He came out of nowhere and took the crown!” EWC posted on social media following the player’s triumph.

In Friday’s second group stage, Zubair decisively defeated another Pakistani eSpo­rts icon and Tekken star — Lahore-born Arslan “Ash” Siddique — before once again beating the eight-time Evolution Championship Series (Evo) winner in a thrilling 5-4 semifinal on Saturday. Arslan is one of Pakistan’s most prominent esports figures and one of the leading names in the global fighting game community.

Advancing into the grand final, Zubair faced off against LowHigh in a decisively less close game, sweeping his opponent with a 5-0 victory.

The newly-crowned World Champion was awarded a cash prize of $250,000.

Ash, meanwhile, settled for fourth place after losing the decider to Australia’s Yagami.

In June, he had won the 2026 Evo series in Las Vegas, considered the world’s largest fighting game tournament, with his fourth consecutive title.

Tekken is a world-renowned video game with a massive following. Other ongoing and completed tournaments at the EWC include Call of Duty: Black Ops 7, Counter Strike 2, Dota 2, League of Legends, Street Fighter, and Valorant.

World.title: Flour prices rising as govt yet to issue import tender
World.content:
KARACHI: Consumers continued to face rising prices for wheat and wheat flour as the federal government plans to import one million tonnes of grain to curb the escalating costs.

According to the Sensitive Price Index data as at Aug 6, the prices of 20 kg wheat flour, 10 kg wheat bag and one kg fine flour have further increased in Karachi to Rs2,700-3,000, Rs1,200 and Rs158.56, up from Rs2,600-2,900, Rs1,160 and Rs149.46, respectively, prevailing at the week ending July 30.

The national average prices of a 20 kg flour bag, 10 kg wheat, and 1 kg fine flour for the week ending Aug 6 were Rs2,200-3,133, Rs1,235, and Rs153, as compared to Rs2,200-3,133, Rs1,223, and Rs152.14 for the week ending July 30. In the above period, wheat flour price has risen by 0.52pc.

Traders said that the government is not paying any attention to the rising prices of wheat and wheat flour ahead of one million wheat imports. If the government does not bother to control prices before the arrival of imported wheat, consumers will not derive any substantial benefit from this decision.

As per SPI data, in Islamabad and Rawalpindi, 10 kg wheat bag prices are the highest at Rs1,339.31, forcing consumers to pay Rs3,040-3,133 for a 20 kg wheat flour bag, followed by Rs173.68 per kg of fine flour, compared to other cities.

As provinces are outlining their plans and requirements for wheat, the Sindh Cabinet on Wednesday approved the import of 500,000 tonnes of wheat through the Trading Corporation of Pakistan under the framework being coordinated by the federal government.

Punjab plans to import one million tonnes followed by 200,000 tonnes by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and 57,500 tonnes by Balochistan.

Karachi Wholesalers Grocers Association (KWGA) Chairman Rauf Ibrahim said the government needs to expedite its efforts to curb wheat hoarding by vested interests and speculators who have already plunged into the commodity business.

He said the government is taking too long to issue a tender for wheat imports, as it will take a few months for imported wheat to reach Pakistan, while the new wheat crops will arrive in March-May 2027.

Published in Dawn, August 9th, 2026

World.title: Pakistan bags three medals at Nuclear Science Olympiad
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: A Pakis­tan team has won one gold and two silver medals at the 3rd International Nuclear Science Olympiad (INSO-2026), held in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia from Aug 2 to 8.

Supported by the Inter­national Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), the competition brought together around 120 students and experts from 19 countries, including China, Japan, Russia, Turkiye, Malaysia, Indonesia, and Saudi Arabia.

The team was selected and trained by the Pakis­tan Institute of Engi­neer­ing and Applied Sciences (PIEAS), under the auspi­ces of the Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission (PAEC).

Muhammad Ali from Govt College University, Lahore, won a gold medal, while Muhammad Usman from F.G. Sir Syed College, The Mall, Rawalpindi, and Seerat Fatima from Nixor College, Karachi, secured silver medals. Syed Shuja Haider from Sundar STEM School, Lahore, also represented Pakistan at the Olympiad.

The students were selec­­ted through the Pakis­tan Nuclear Science Olymp­ia­­­d, an initiative of PAEC ai­­m­ed at identifying and nurturing young scientific talent for participation in the International Nuclear Science Olympiad.

In another developme­­nt, Pakistan was annou­n­ced as the host of the 4th In­­ternational Nuclear Sci­ence Olympiad in 2027.

On the occasion, Dr Mu­­hammad Maqsood from the PAEC Directorate of Edu­cation and Dr Sajjad Tahir from PIEAS received a commemorative memento.
